I have farmed these 3 mu in Quzhou for 40 years, and finishing high school taught me to think about the soil balance, not just habit. But this is still a small farm — my sons work in Shijiazhuang, so it is mainly me and my sister-in-law in the fields. Every jin of fertilizer is cash out of my pocket, and with only 3 mu, one bad crop means the year is ruined. I start from what I did last year and change only what I can justify.

For winter wheat, I sow Jimai 22, an improved variety, at 12.5 kg per mu in early October. Our soil here is loamy and irrigable, but after summer maize it needs rebuilding. At sowing I put down a base dressing that gives 8 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. Then at jointing in late March I topdress another 8 kg nitrogen per mu as urea, bringing the total to 16 kg nitrogen. I have tried 14 kg before, and the wheat yellowed at the second node — I will not risk that again for the sake of 10 yuan. I irrigate three times: the overwinter water in mid-November, the jointing water in late March, and one at grain filling in mid-May. A fourth irrigation costs 15 yuan per mu in electricity and might add 20 kg of grain at most, so it does not pay. I rotary till before sowing because the maize stubble must be chopped or the drill chokes. Two pesticide applications: one broadleaf herbicide in early spring, and one fungicide-insecticide mix at heading to stop rust and aphids. I expect 500 kg per mu.

For summer maize, I plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid at 2.5 kg per mu right after wheat harvest in mid-June. The window is narrow — if I wait two extra days, the yield drops. So I use no-tillage direct seeding into the wheat stubble to save time and diesel. At sowing I apply 5 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu in the seed furrow, then side-dress 10 kg nitrogen per mu at the seven-leaf stage in mid-July. That is 15 kg nitrogen total. I irrigate twice: at the seven-leaf stage and at tasseling. More water just invites lodging in our clay-loam patches. Two sprays: a pre-emergence herbicide immediately after sowing, and one insecticide at the heart-leaf stage for corn borer. I expect 550 kg per mu.

I watch the neighbors on this lane. Most use 15 to 17 kg nitrogen on wheat and 14 to 16 kg on maize. I sit at the upper end of that because I would rather spend an extra 25 yuan per mu on fertilizer than lose 50 kg of grain. A 3-mu farm cannot absorb a yield failure. At the same time, I do not buy foliar fertilizers or growth regulators — they are optional, and on a small farm optional means skip. The money saved goes to the two days of hired harvest labor I need in June and September.
